(1) the prevalence of diabetes mellitus (DM) is high among patients undergoing hemodialysis (HD) in Taiwan; (2) the incidence of DM is high in patients undergoing HD in Taiwan; (3) the incidence of cardiovascular diseases and all-cause mortality are high among patients undergoing HD in the Taiwan population; (4) the prevalence of DM and the incidence of cardiovascular disease and all-cause death were higher among patients undergoing HD than among the general population; (5)

the administration of thiamine and vitamin B6 in patients undergoing hemodialysis is associated with an improvement in oxidative stress, inflammation, and endothelial dysfunction markers and with an attenuation of the formation of advanced glycation end-products.
high-dose thia-mine and pyrid-oxine administration to hemodialysis patients reduces AGEs and other markers of oxidative stress and inflammation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of thiamine and/or pyridoxine supplementation on the level of AGEs and other oxidative stress parameters in hemodialysis (HD) patients.
the effect of high-dose vitamin B6 and thiamine supplementation on oxidative stress markers and advanced glycation end-products (AGEs) in hemodialysis (HD) patients.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the evidence is not strong enough to recommend high-dose thioamin and pyridoxin for patients with CKD.
the effect of thiamine and other B vitamins on the development of cardiovascular diseases in the general population is still uncertain and requires more research.
the effect of vitamin B6 on blood pressure is not clear.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
our results show that the use of high-dose vitamins (thiamine and pyri-doxine) in patients with end-stage renal disease (ESRD) and diabetes mellitus (DM) on hemodialysis (HD) is safe.
the effect of thiamine and vitamin B6 on oxidative stress markers in HD patients has been shown to be significant and beneficial.
we have shown a strong association between the presence of the 3p24.1 deletion and the development of B cell malignancies, particularly CLL.
The main takeaway from our work is that
high-dose B vitamin supplements can reduce advanced glycation end-product (AGE) levels in patients undergoing hemodialysis.
thiamine and B6 can be used as adjunctive therapy for patients with CKD.
we need to be more aware of the potential for adverse effects when prescribing high doses of B6.
